_comment: AE4.9 / ADR 0176 D5 — THE ENFORCEMENT MANIFEST. NO DEFAULT ARM.
Source of truth for this file's SHAPE and gates: docs/decisions/0176-...-made-real.md D5.
Generator: scripts/gen-authz-matrix-cells.mjs   Emits: authz_enforcement_manifest.psql
Catalog binding: supabase/tests/410_ae49_d5_enforcement_manifest.sql (post-reset pgTAP).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. 401 § 19 used to map 43 permission codes to their legacy gate with a
`CASE ... ELSE 'is_staff_admin_of_for'`. That ELSE sent 38 of 43 codes to one gate, so a 44th
permission would have INHERITED a mapping instead of forcing a decision. Every row here is
explicit; there is no wildcard key, no `??` fallback on the generator's read path, and every
required field is read through a `req()` helper that THROWS when the key is absent. A 44th
permission breaks `npm run lint:authz-vectors` until someone names its enforcement path.
THE DIVISION OF LABOUR, AND WHY IT IS SPLIT THIS WAY (the binding constraint):
* `npm run lint` (gate 12) is PURE JSON. It must never require Docker. It checks that this
file is internally consistent, has no default arm, and agrees with `catalogSnapshot`.
* `supabase/tests/410_...sql` checks `catalogSnapshot` against the LIVE CATALOG, both set
differences, in a place where the DB is already up. That is where the catalog is truth.
Neither half alone closes the loop, and the snapshot is the seam between them: lint proves the
manifest matches the snapshot, 410 proves the snapshot matches the database.
PROVENANCE IS DECLARED PER FIELD, DELIBERATELY. Some of what a row declares is bound to the
catalog (`catalog.*`, asserted by 410); some is derived from a written architecture rule
(`axes.resourceLifecycle`); some is measured off a site body (`hardDenyClasses` where sites are
enumerated); and some is HONESTLY NOT YET KNOWABLE (`not-attributable-until-rekey`). Collapsing
those into one undifferentiated list would let an unmeasured field read exactly like a measured
one. The escape hatch is FENCED: `not-attributable-until-rekey` is admissible ONLY on a row with
zero enumerated sites AND a reviewed call-graph boundary, so it can never silence a row whose
sites are known.
⛔⛔ AND THE MEASURED LABEL CARRIES ITS DEPTH IN ITS NAME — READ IT BEFORE READING A ZERO.
`measured-depth1-at-sites-and-authorizer` (3 rows) means EXACTLY: no hard-deny vocabulary gate
is invoked DIRECTLY in an enumerated site body or in the domain authorizer body. It says NOTHING
about the composed-call closure below those bodies, and its empty `hardDenyClasses` is therefore
A BOUND, NOT AN ABSENCE. Renamed from `measured-at-declared-sites` 2026-09-03 (review F-MAJOR-1
remediation (a)) precisely because the old name read as a closure it never had.
MEASURED ON THE LIVE CATALOG 2026-09-03, comments stripped, depth 1 = the bodies 410 §6.2
searches — `principal_inactive` (`app.is_active`) IS enforced on ALL THREE of those rows:
* permission arm, all 3 rows: depth 4 — has_permission -> entailed_grants -> assignment_facts
* commission.forms.edit, preserved arm: depth 2 — app.is_tenancy_admin_of_for
* org.professionals.{create,read}, preserved arm: depth 3 — app.is_org_admin_of
* org.professionals.read also reaches `respondent_exclusion` at depth 5, via can_read_case_committee
⚠ The review paraphrase 'depth 2 on both arms' holds for ONE arm of ONE row. Raising the search
by a single hop would catch that one and leave the other five paths unmeasured — a partial fix
that reads as a complete one. The transitive end state is FUP-AE4-HARDDENY-CLASSES-CANNOT-FAIL.
MEASURED 2026-09-02 on the local stack at migration head 20261003007260, read-only, by the
AE4.9 D5 author. RE-DERIVE, NEVER QUOTE. 410 is what proves this current; nothing else does.
The ADR cites head 20261003007240 for its own measurements — this snapshot is LATER, and the
difference is why the head is recorded here rather than assumed to match the ADR.
_permissionsComment: ⭐⭐ THIS LIST IS DELIBERATELY REDUNDANT WITH THE KEYS OF `permissions` BELOW, AND THE
REDUNDANCY IS THE GATE. If the manifest's row keys were their own snapshot, then
`catalog - manifest` and `manifest - catalog` would be the SAME SET compared with itself —
a tautology that passes for any input, which is exactly the vacuity D5 exists to kill. Two
independently-written lists give lint a real difference to compute in both directions, and
410 binds THIS list (not the row keys) to authz.permissions. A 44th permission therefore
reds 410 first; adding it here then reds lint until someone writes its enforcement row.
⛔ Never 'fix' a lint red by regenerating this list from the row keys.

_comment: authz.role_state, MEASURED from the domain's CHECK constraint rather than transcribed from a
migration. `nonLegacy` is the complement of `legacy` and is therefore {test_validation,
authoritative}.
⚠⚠ A DECLARED DIVERGENCE: THIS GATE IS BROADER THAN ITS SPEC, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS
RECORDED HERE BECAUSE NOTHING ELSE WOULD SAY SO. ADR 0176 D5 words its third set difference
as `authoritative roles - approved suites`. The gate enforces that (arm C1 in
scripts/gen-authz-matrix-cells.mjs, and 410 § 7.1) AND ALSO the wider `nonLegacy - approved
suites` (arm C2, and 410 § 7.2), which additionally catches a role parked in
`test_validation`. Broader than spec is the safe direction, but it is still a divergence: a
reader checking the gate against D5 will find an arm D5 does not ask for, and a future
editor might 'correct' it back to the ADR's wording and silently lose the test_validation
half. The justification is that a role under `test_validation` is BEING differentialled —
it owes a suite at least as much as one already authoritative. C1 and C2 are kept as TWO
arms rather than one wide arm so each names its own subject when it fires.
Role -> the approved matrix and the differential suite that measure it. D5's third set
difference is `authoritative roles - approved suites`; the KEYS of this object are the
'approved suites' side of it. Lint fuses these keys to the axes file's `subjectRoles` in BOTH
directions, so the two lists cannot drift apart while each arm reads a different one.
The classes layer 3 composes BEFORE the positive entitlement source (ADR 0176 D2 interface 3).
`gate` names the single function that IS the class where one exists; 410 asserts those
functions exist, so a rename reds here instead of silently emptying the vocabulary.
NOT GATED: 'every vocabulary entry is used by at least one row'. Today 40 of 43 rows carry
`not-attributable-until-rekey` and the 3 rows with enumerated sites measured ZERO hard denies
AT DEPTH 1 — directly in a site body or the authorizer body, which is the whole of what that
label claims. ⚠ At depth 2-5 those same 3 rows DO reach `principal_inactive`, and one reaches
`respondent_exclusion`; the per-row depths are in this file's header. A zero here is the search
horizon, never a finding of absence. So that arm could only be satisfied by FABRICATING
attributions the depth-1 measurement did not make. The unused set is reported as
a statistic in authz-matrix-coverage.json instead of being gated into existence.

fetched with `req()`, which throws on absence — that is the structural reason a row cannot

_residualLegacyAuthorityComment: ⛔⛔ WHY THIS FIELD EXISTS — IMPOSED AS A CONDITION BY THE LEAD, 2026-09-02, on the ruling
that a re-keyed policy calls ONLY its authorizer.
`re-keyed` DOES NOT MEAN `fully permission-keyed`, and a countdown that reads it that way
LIES. Every one of the three re-keyed authorizers is a DISJUNCTION: one arm is the
permission check, and the others still grant on a role/identity path with NO permission
grant involved. Before the re-key those arms sat in the policy body, where anyone auditing
`pg_policies` for surviving legacy authority would see them. Now they are inside a
SECURITY DEFINER function — invisible to exactly that audit. That is the door-blindness
shape this program keeps paying for (ADR 0079), so the disclosure is DATA, gated, rather
than a sentence in a commit message.
The gate: every entry in `domainAuthorizer.composedWith` must be EITHER the permission arm
(`authz.has_permission`) OR declared here with a population and a retirement condition. A
new arm added to an authorizer cannot slip in unclassified. 410 § 4.6 pins the count of
re-keyed rows that still carry residual authority, so `re-keyed: 3` can never be read as
⚠ The disclosure is owed on ALL THREE re-keyed rows, not only the one the ruling was about:
can_create_professional keeps its org-manager arm and can_read_professional_profile keeps
three arms, one of which is MEASURED OPEN AND MASKING on the seed.

_comment: HOW `axes.resourceLifecycle` WAS DERIVED, stated so a reader can check it instead of trusting
it. Axis 6b's vocabulary (authz-matrix-axes.json) names exactly three resource families: the
FORM VERSION family (draft / published / archived), the RESPONSE family (in_progress /
submitted) and document drafts. A permission that acts on none of those families takes
`not_applicable`, and that is a DERIVATION FROM THE AXIS'S OWN VOCABULARY, not a guess —
provenance `axis-vocabulary-inapplicable`. The ten permissions that DO act on those families
take their values from written architecture rules (Rule 3 lifecycle/resume, Rule 4 sign-offs
only while in_progress, Rule 5 published-version immutability, the dashboard-countable =
submitted filter) — provenance `architecture-rule`.
LIMIT, NAMED RATHER THAN ROUNDED UP: there is NO catalog column encoding lifecycle, so 410
asserts NOTHING about these values. They are an internal-consistency subject only. This is the
one field in a row that no gate can contradict; `po-approved` is reserved for when AE4.3-style
approval gives them an oracle.

_comment: AE4 GATE REPRESENTATIVE 1 of 3 (ADR 0176 D6, PO-confirmed 2026-09-02).
⛔⛔ THE SECOND AUTHORITY MOVED, AND THIS ROW IS THE RECORD OF WHERE IT WENT.
BEFORE the re-key every one of the four policies read `app.is_staff_admin_of(...) OR
app.is_tenancy_admin_of(...)`. AFTER it each policy is a single
`app.can_edit_commission_forms(...)` call — the policy bodies genuinely lost the
tenancy arm — and the arm reappears INSIDE the authorizer, additionally renamed to the
`_for` variant. Both halves matter and neither is visible from the other level:
* per-site `composedWith` now names the authorizer, which is all the site carries;
* row-level `domainAuthorizer.composedWith` names the tenancy arm, and 410 § 3.7
asserts it is still inside the authorizer. Deleting it there is now the regression,
and no site-level assertion could see that.
⚠ THE RENAME IS WHY THE MATCH IS `name || '('`. A substring match for
`app.is_tenancy_admin_of` would have matched `app.is_tenancy_admin_of_for(` as a PREFIX
and reported the old name as still present. Recording the exact called name and
matching it as a CALL is what keeps a rename visible.
✅ FOUND BY THE GATE, NOT BY REVIEW: 410 § 3.5 red on the first run against the re-keyed
catalog. The tripwire and the composition assertion did their jobs on day one.
⛔⛔ SIX SITES, NOT FOUR — BUG-AE49-D6-REKEY-INCOMPLETE, AND WHY THE LIST WAS SHORT.
20261003007300 re-pointed FOUR policies and this row declared exactly those four with
`status: re-keyed` and `callGraphBoundary: null` — i.e. it claimed a COMPLETE site list.
The PO-approved matrix (docs/design/authz-ae43-staff-admin-permission-matrix.md:291) names
SEVEN, and two of them — `form_item_options_staff_admin_write` and
`form_item_validations_staff_admin_write` — still carried the pre-cutover predicate
verbatim. NOTHING RED: 410's set differences ran on the PERMISSION axis, and the SITE axis
had no closure check in either direction (FUP-AE4-MANIFEST-HAS-NO-SITE-AXIS-CLOSURE).
20261003007340 re-points the two, and 410 § 8 is the arm that can now see the shape.
⚠ THE TWO ARE NOT EQUALLY REACHABLE. Measured grants: `authenticated` holds full DML on
`form_item_options` (a LIVE door) and SELECT ONLY on `form_item_validations` — whose
policy is therefore a BACKSTOP no PostgREST write can reach, its real write path being
the SECURITY DEFINER `public.set_item_validations`, which is still layer-1 and carries no
permission-code literal. Both are declared here because both are enforcement sites of
this code; 409 § 2.6d/2.6e assert the opposite postures and § 2.10c pins the door's
un-re-keyed state as a countdown. ⛔ Do not read this row's completeness as "the
commission.forms.edit write path is fully permission-keyed": the POLICY sites are, the
DEFINER doors (matrix row 1's "D 8 form fns", measured 0-of-8 carrying a code) are not.
⚠ THE SEVENTH MATRIX NAME IS NOT A POLICY. `form_block_library` carries NO write policy of
any kind — measured on the live catalog: `authenticated` holds SELECT and nothing else on
the table (table AND column grants), and every write goes through one of THREE SECURITY
DEFINER doors (save_block_to_library / update_block_library_entry /
delete_block_library_entry, plus insert_block_from_library which reads it). So it is a
`D` site, not an `R` site, and it is NOT listed here: those four doors gate on
`app.is_staff_admin_of(...) OR app.is_tenancy_admin_of(...)` and carry NO permission-code
literal, so they are pending-rekey, not enforcement sites for this code. Correcting matrix
row 1 is filed as review finding F-REC-4 and is the PO's edit, not this file's.
